verdict.rationale: Pipecat is a framework for building voice AI agents, so consuming tools from MCP servers is a fair question to ask of it. However, nothing in the evidence shows Pipecat agents connecting to MCP servers as a client. The only MCP mention is context-hub, which registers Pipecat's docs index as an MCP server for a coding agent; that is the opposite role. Flows functions that call external APIs are an adjacent feature and earn no credit here.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools
